title: DLO to DMO: Canonical Modeling Before Unification

steps.prompt: An ERP connector will land millions of party/order rows into Data 360. Architects must preserve source fidelity for reprocessing, expose a canonical Individual model for identity resolution, and later may replace a Contact DLO or install packaged Sales data kits. What modeling discipline is required?

options.label: Ingest into Data Lake Objects (DLO), map fields to standard Data Model Objects (DMO), and maintain verified primary key lineage
options.rationale: Staging data in DLOs preserves raw source fidelity, while mapping to standardized DMOs establishes the canonical layer required for identity resolution and modular stream replacement.

options.label: Ingest ERP streams directly into Unified Individual DMOs, bypassing intermediate Data Lake Objects to maximize ingest speed
options.distractorAntipattern: Ingesting directly into DMOs is technically impossible in Data 360 and destroys raw source auditability.
options.rationale: Data 360 architecture requires streams to land in DLOs first; bypassing DLO staging prevents raw data reprocessing and breaks platform lineage.

options.label: Unmap the active Contact DLO primary key from Individual before creating the new replacement stream to avoid mapping conflicts
options.distractorAntipattern: Unmapping primary keys from populated DMOs breaks downstream identity resolution rulesets and calculated insights.
options.rationale: Severing primary key mappings on active DMOs causes immediate failures across dependent identity resolution jobs and downstream calculated insights.

options.label: Deploy the packaged Sales Data Kit over existing custom DLO-to-DMO mappings to automatically standardize harmonized definitions
options.distractorAntipattern: Overwriting custom DLO-to-DMO mappings with default data kit templates silently breaks bespoke field mappings.
options.rationale: Deploying packaged data kits over customized DLO-DMO configurations overwrites custom relationships and breaks downstream segmentation and activation.
